svg.text: Stage 1 of the v10 architecture: AI-assisted translation & candidate interpretation, from raw utterance to human-approved meaning
AI proposes → models compare & disagree → humans interpret & validate → local concept first → semantic mappings only after approval
FARAJAMH MINORITY REPORT — AI candidate generation & disagreement detection (never decides)
LOCAL CONCEPT LAYER (stage 2.5) — written only after a final decision
• Create a concept or add a variant (dialect, region, spelling); approved translation and meaning
• clinical_status: non-clinical cultural / possible indicator / symptom expression / safety-relevant
• Valid even with no external concept. Holds meaning, not patient data.
CONCEPT DECISION per approved meaning (v10 stages 3–4)
• approve → predicate (exact / broad / narrow / related) + reviewer confidence
• reject with 'Not' → recorded negative mapping (e.g. bewitchment ≠ persecutory delusion)
• no adequate concept → semantic gap (not a failure) defer → nothing leaves the package
exact / broad → candidate 'Maps to' a standard concept; related & gaps → local custom concept
(ID > 2 billion). Which predicates produce 'Maps to' is to be agreed with the OMOP team.
approved local concepts feed M3 context & triage (versioned)
WHAT EACH LAYER HOLDS — kept separate so any output can be traced back and reviewed
Only L9 leaves the DSA-approved environment. L1–L8 form the audit trail: package JSON + decisions, hashed and versioned with the run.
GUARDS ENFORCED IN CODE (policy/farajamh_mr_odrl.jsonld, which extends the upstream ODRL policy)
Restricted data → only local, DSA-approved model hosts (upstream Gemini CLI path off)
Safety-flagged utterances blocked until escalation is recorded
Concept IDs only from terminology-service responses; invented IDs dropped
No winner: minority readings retained and labelled
No SSSOM, local concept or OMOP row without a final human decision; placeholders refused
